absent: Locking discipline and allocation lifetime for PnP cards devices protocols and identifier chains.
Implementation of protocol resource control and suspend resume and driver probe remove paths.
Error values and side effects for enabled build PnP configuration start stop and reservation checks.
Synchronization and sizing for PPS event queue and async notification and removal handling.
Persistent reservation semantics for registration preemption fencing and generation handling.
ACL permission evaluation and xattr encode decode rules outside size and count helpers.
Namespace install and ownership rules and inode number allocation outside the fallback stub.

findings.text: Card object combines driver model membership with identity and inventory state. It carries a small numeric index meant to be unique, three list nodes for global collection and protocol collection and attached devices, references to owning protocol and identifier chain, a readable label plus version serial and checksum fields, and proc directory linkage. Conversions derive a card from its global node or protocol node or embedded device, and iteration walks the global card collection.

Device object groups driver model linkage and DMA mask with indexing and status, four list nodes for global and protocol and card and requested device collections, back references to protocol and card and driver and card linkage, identifier chain, activation and capability state with dependent set count plus resource and option lists, readable label with protocol private flags and opaque data, and proc entry linkage. Helpers derive a device from global or card or protocol nodes or embedded device, walk global or per card collections, expose the label, and proxy driver private storage through the embedded device.

Link object pairs a card with its card driver, holding opaque driver storage and power state, with small accessors for that storage. Fixup object pairs a short identifier with a callback invoked for quirks on a device.

Identifier node holds fixed length EISA text plus next pointer. Device driver descriptor holds name and identifier table and flags, lifecycle callbacks for probe and remove and shutdown and suspend and resume, and embedded driver model driver with conversion helper. Card driver descriptor holds global list node and name and card identifier table and flags, callbacks for probe and remove and suspend and resume over a card link, and an embedded device driver used as link with conversion helper.

Protocol descriptor holds list membership and name, resource control callbacks for retrieval and setting and disabling, wakeup query plus suspend and resume, and layer owned state comprising numeric protocol identity and driver model linkage and card and device collections. Helpers convert a list node to a protocol and walk per protocol cards or devices.

Configuration mode named normal equals 0x0001 while forced mode equals 0x0002 and skips validity checks. Driver resource policy for leaving state unchanged equals 0x0001 while policy for leaving device disabled equals 0x0003.
Device capability flags use distinct single bit values. Read equals 0x0001, write equals 0x0002, disable equals 0x0004, configurable equals 0x0008, removable equals 0x0010, console equals 0x0020.
Operational state codes are ready with value 0x0000, attached with value 0x0001, busy with value 0x0002, faulty with value 0x0004.

Read and write and disable and configure and suspend eligibility combine capability bits with callback availability and activation or console policy. Read needs retrieval support and read bit, write needs setting support and write bit, disable needs disabling support and disable bit with console devices further gated by console suspend enablement, configuration needs an inactive device and configurable bit, suspend needs suspend support with the same console gating.

Protocol identity checks compare a device protocol pointer against well known protocol objects for ISA PnP and PnP BIOS and ACPI, returning the associated ACPI object or null. Alternate build variants replace these checks with constant false or zero and report BIOS support as disabled. ISA card helpers expose the owning card number or negative one when unattached and expose the device number as slot number.

Device lifecycle distinguishes ready and attached and busy and faulty codes plus a separate active flag. Configuration is permitted only while inactive. Driver resource flags select leaving the device alone versus forcing disabled. Status and active interact with capability gates to decide attach and configure and start and suspend paths.

Extension points are device driver probe and remove and shutdown and suspend and resume, card driver probe and remove and suspend and resume over card links, protocol retrieval and setting and disabling and wakeup and suspend and resume, and fixup quirk invoked on a device. Card probe receives a link plus matched identifier and device probe receives a device plus matched identifier.

When the feature is compiled out, attach reports a missing device and detach does nothing with platform device count zero, card device lookup returns null while release and unregister do nothing, registration and automatic configuration and start and stop and activate and disable report a missing device, possible configuration and range reservation report success with zero, active test reports false, identifier comparison reports a missing device, and device identity test reports false.
Helper macro wires a driver object to registration and unregistration through the generic module driver facility.

Poison pointer base is either a configured illegal pointer value or zero depending on build. Derived invalid pointers add fixed offsets to that base. List markers use 0x100 and 0x122, timer static uses 0x300, tail mapping uses 0x400, mutex wait context uses 0x500, protection signature uses 0x40, skb list next uses 0x800, net pointer uses 0x801, BPF uses 0xEB9F, virtual filesystem uses 0xF5, stack depot uses 0xD390, io_uring uses 0x1091.

Poison bytes use page value 0xaa, allocator inactive 0xbb and active 0xcc, in use 0x5a and free 0x6b with end marker 0xa5, init memory free 0xcc, journal 0x5b and journal2 0x5c, pool freed 0xa7 and allocated 0xa9, ATM free 0x12 and ATM word 0xdeadbeef, mutex init 0x11 and free 0x22, key destroy 0xbd.

Invalid poison pointers are intended to fault if dereferenced after freeing or misuse. Forced configuration bypasses validity checks. Console capability restricts disable and suspend unless console suspend is enabled. Disabled build stubs report absence or success with zero, so callers must handle null and missing device and false identity without assuming hardware access.

Access control entry holds tag and permission plus an identifier that is either user or group. Access control list header groups reference count and entry count and deferred free linkage, followed by a flexible entry array counted by the stored count. Iteration walks from the first entry up to first plus count.

Duplication increments the reference count when an object is present and returns the same pointer. Release decrements and on last reference schedules deferred freeing through RCU. Cached ACL clearing stores nulls for access and default on inodes in the enabled build and does nothing in the fallback build.

Fallback build reports chmod and creation and listing as success with zero and null outputs, disables simple setting, drops cache and forget operations to no action, and reports set and get and remove extended operations as unsupported.

On disk size equals header size plus count times entry size. Count validation rejects buffers smaller than a header or with a remainder after removing the header, otherwise divides the remainder by entry size. Name mapping returns access or default extended attribute names by type and empty otherwise, with reverse mapping returning access or default or negative one. Decoding from extended attributes in this build reports unsupported.

Source description holds symbolic name and device path, allowed mode, echo callback, owner and parent device. Event time holds real timestamp and optionally raw timestamp when NTP PPS is enabled. Device object combines source description and current parameters, assert and clear sequence counters with timestamped values plus mode at event, last and last fetched event identifiers, wait queue, numeric identifier and lookup cookie, driver model linkage, asynchronous notification queue, spin protection, and removal flag.

Conversion copies seconds and nanoseconds from broken down time into PPS timestamp fields. Sampling captures real time and, when NTP PPS is enabled, also monotonic raw time from a single snapshot. Subtraction removes a delta from real and, when enabled, raw components.

PPS device carries a spinlock alongside its wait queue and async queue, indicating event state is protected by spinning while wakeups are distributed through queueing. ACL lifetime uses reference counting with RCU deferred reclamation rather than explicit locking in these fragments. PnP global and protocol and card lists show no acquisition order here, so external serialization must be defined elsewhere.

Key listing holds generation and count followed by a flexible key array. Held reservation holds key and generation and type. Operation table offers registration and reservation and release and preemption and clearing and key reading and reservation reading. Key reading requires a caller sized array with capacity in the count field, and the callee updates count to the total present even when truncated so the caller can retry larger.

Persistent reservation operations are invoked per block device with keys and types and flags. PPS echo is invoked on events with device and event identifier and opaque data. Namespace operations offer per task acquisition and release and installation into a set and owner lookup and parent lookup.

Generator state holds four 32 bit words. Seeding folds 64 bit input through shifts and exclusive or into a 32 bit intermediate then derives each word through lower bound enforcement with thresholds two and eight and sixteen and 128. One time initialization guards full seeding to run once per per cpu state.

Stride equals four times level one cache line size. Range prefetch iterates from start to end by stride issuing prefetch when architecture support is present, otherwise doing nothing. Page address prefetch only prefetches under virtual addressability builds.

Namespace operations table holds name and real name plus callbacks for per task acquisition and release and installation into a set and owner lookup and parent lookup, with layout randomization annotation. Initial inode numbers alias per type init constants for IPC and UTS and user and PID and cgroup and time and net and mount. Inode to namespace conversion reads the private pointer. Fallback allocator returns one and success while freeing does nothing.
Spin begin and end are empty, while CPU relax in spin loops maps directly to generic CPU relax.
Each header defines a private include guard macro so repeated inclusion has no further effect.
